description.narrative:
This needs analysis is based on the following evidence: Oxfam’s own assessments including a Rapid Gender Analysis (March-May 2024),Protection Analysis (August 2024), Rapid Needs Assessment in North Gaza (September 2024), and Food Security and Livelihoods Assessment in Tulkarem (July-August 2024), research papers (e.g. ‘Water War Crimes’, July 2024), as well as secondary data and information from interagency/cluster coordination and publications. The situation and needs in Gaza and West Bank are changingand worsening daily; the needs analysis therefore gives an overview of the needs at the time of writing.
Oxfam’s Rapid Needs Assessment found that the top three priorities for people are food (88 %), followed by WASH (72%) and health services (48%). Other priorities include electricity (Gaza is under blackout since the start of the war), livelihoods and NFIs. Shockingly, only 20% of sites in North Gaza reported receiving humanitarian assistance, highlighting how Israel’s movement restrictions and insecurity limit humanitarian organisationsin accessing people in need. These limitations also apply to humanitarian organisations working in Southern Gaza, where additionally hardly any humanitarian or commercial cargo – including fuel - is arriving as of September 2024, severely affecting humanitarian interventions and basic service provision, let alone the market in Gaza.
The gendered impacts of this crisis span across all humanitarian sectors and impact all levels of the population in Gaza. According to Oxfam and our partners’ Rapid Gender Analysis conducted in March-May 2024 across the Gaza Strip, 83% of respondents highlighted that roles of family members have significantly changed during the war. Widowed women take on all roles that support the family’s basic needs and became the breadwinners for their immediate and extended family; men became the ones tasked with shopping and leaving the shelter to look for food, water and fuel. Women generally take tasks inside and outside the shelter such as cooking, food preparation and childcare, whilst men tend to take on tasks outside of their homes. Children and young adults who have been out of school and university since the start of the war now cover the adult roles (searching for food and water, cooking,cleaning) and care work. Gazans, especially women and girls, today spend hours queuing for aid, fuel, water, healthcare, and taking care of their families – all unpaid. Care work is made harder for both women and men by the overall lack of materials forchildcare and the household, availability of clean and sufficient water as well as the many risks involved by leaving the shelter to collect or buy items of daily use such as firewood (as cooking gas is largely not available anymore).

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam Novib has been active in the Occupied Palestinian Territory/Israel (OPT/I) since 1982 and working with Palestinian refugees in Lebanon since the mid 1980s. It has built up a strong network of relationships with local NGOs and counts among its localcounterparts some of the largest and most professional NGOs in various sectors. It has accompanied these NGOs in their development from ad hoc volunteer groups to sizeable professional institutions with national outreach. At the same time the conceptualisation of the programme has evolved from three country programs in the early 1990s to a program for Palestinians in the Middle East (PME) working withPalestinians in OPT, Israel and Lebanon.
The programme has changed over the years with the establishment of the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the mid-1990s from a focus on support and service provision at a grassroots level and grassroots mobilization, to working towards influencing the establishment of the PA, its lawmaking and supporting building a democratic state # this involved supporting efforts of Palestinian civil society to build the basis for a democratic Palestinian state with room for civil participation, ensuring inclusion of vulnerable groups, refugees and women, and shaping its laws and systems. Oxfam Novib has also supported partners that are working on the provision of humanitarian assistance, response preparedness and conflict transformation. We have also supported partners in the provision of health services, access to quality education and gender justice.
